A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same projection-sharing study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison after matching renamed variants and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-task, vision, anomaly-detection, and language-model experiments, including downstream accuracy and inference benchmarks. The separately attributed medical-segmentation results are not needed for this judgment.

after.justification: v3 retains the original language-model and inference experiments and reports revised synthetic and vision outcomes, including additional TinyImageNet variant results.

M1.justification: The three projection-sharing constraints, optional 2D positional injection, and combinations with GQA/MQA remain unchanged. Q-K=V and Q=K-V become Q≠K=V and Q=K≠V; the definitions and attention equations establish that these are notation changes.

E1.justification: The same five synthetic tasks, vision datasets, set-anomaly task, SlimPajama training data, and downstream language benchmarks remain. Additional variants on TinyImageNet and revised sampling within existing tasks do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The TinyImageNet comparison expands from QKV, Q=K-V, and Q=K=V to all six existing variants, adding Q≠K=V and both positional-injection variants in Table 3. Synthetic diagnostic comparisons also expand from three to six variants. The external baseline families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The classification grid now fixes patch size, learning rate, and depth while narrowing embedding dimensions. TinyImageNet changes from curves extending to 100 epochs in v1 to a stated 20-epoch protocol. Appendix A.3.2 replaces the anomaly experiment's split and per-image epoch description with 10,000 sampled training sets and 2,000 test-derived evaluation sets, and changes model dimensions and learning rate. The replacement synthetic convergence diagnostic specifies ten epochs; its sequence length is inconsistently labeled 64 in the plot and 16 in the caption.

E4.justification: The synthetic diagnostic evidence is substantially revised: v1 Figures 3–4 compare three variants, whereas v3 Figures 2–3 compare six. Training/validation losses against elapsed time are replaced by training losses against epochs, and new attention maps examine projection sharing and positional injection across four tasks, omitting the previous SUB maps. The TinyImageNet training/validation curves are removed. The language-model context-length analysis remains unchanged.

E5.justification: TinyImageNet explicitly changes from two runs per variant to one. The previous two-repeat statements for other vision classification and anomaly experiments disappear, without establishing their replacement run counts. The new synthetic convergence figure explicitly reports means over three seeds; the main synthetic experiment already reported three runs. No confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 are extensively replaced. Synthetic average accuracy changes from 0.851 to 0.758 for QKV and from 0.854 to 0.724 for shared-query/key attention. Vision's highest average switches from the positional shared-query/key variant to its unaugmented version. TinyImageNet adds three result entries, and QKV accuracy changes from 0.229 to 0.331 under revised settings, not a demonstrated same-setting gain. Synthetic diagnostic findings change, while the language-model and attributed segmentation tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The attention equations, complexity expressions, linear-attention/state-space derivation in Appendix A.1, and positional-encoding construction in Appendix A.2 are retained. No mathematical definitions, proofs, or formal results are substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims: projection sharing can preserve quality, K=V halves the cache, projection sharing complements head sharing, and usefulness depends on the task. Revised wording and supporting non-language results do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 expands the interpretation of synthetic results, attributing differences on REVERSE and SWAP to routing constraints and positional injection. For TinyImageNet, further training is now suggested to separate architectures rather than close their performance gap. Section 6 explicitly disclaims universal optimality of K=V, while the new summary table recommends it as a default QKV replacement.

D1.justification: New disclosures include CIFAR crop/flip augmentation, frozen precomputed 512-dimensional ResNet34 features, and TinyImageNet fp16 training and revised timing information. Previous anomaly dropout and warmup-scheduler details disappear. The code-access pointer changes from the anushamadan02 repository to Brainchip-Inc. Appendix A.5's language-model configuration remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier projection sharing, GQA/MQA, MLA, and efficient attention remain unchanged. The reference lists match; the code-link change does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes variant notation, makes local language corrections, and rewrites portions of the synthetic and vision discussion and anomaly protocol. Appendix A.6 adds a short summary. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Synthetic curves and attention maps are substantially redesigned, including expanded variant displays, new axes, legends, and captions. The TinyImageNet figure is removed, Table 3 uses compact horizontal headers, and existing language-model curves are enlarged into stacked plots on separate pages. The segmentation table is relocated beside its diagram, and Table 17 adds a qualitative summary of existing findings.

improvement.justification: Broader TinyImageNet variant comparisons, clearer diagnostic displays, and additional implementation details provide benefits. However, TinyImageNet repetitions fall from two to one, validation and timing diagnostics disappear, and v3 Figure 2 contradicts itself about sequence length: 64 in the plot versus 16 in its caption. With the main method and language-model evidence unchanged, these gains and reporting weaknesses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
